about: The owner's rulings of 22 Nov 2026 applied to the rows of docs/research/baggage-claims-content-proposal.csv that had been left for him, in the Concept, Research, Marketing and Sales stages and the website platform, with the lines, voice packs and channels he asked for. A question or a decision is "decided" only where his own words decide it, and the row quotes them (`ruling`). Figures he asked to have guessed are labelled as estimates with what they rest on. Everything else is entered at its lowest status; claims stay unverified. Rows are added once per database by src/lib/seedContentDb.ts; a row a person has changed is left alone.

match.title: Which web stack for the product site?

rows.appendBody: Decided by the owner on 22 Nov 2026: the product's own site runs on this app's stack; Stripe for the site, Amazon marketplace for the listing; the product's own mail server, set in Admin; the referral engine built in; no Shopify. The stack is Next.js, React, Tailwind and PostgreSQL with pgvector, with files and embeddings kept in PostgreSQL. rows.title: Why now
rows.body: The PRD's case: the US gifts, novelty and souvenir market was worth about $32.7B in 2025 and is forecast to grow at about 6.4% a year through 2034; gag gifting is a proven $12-15 consumer price band on Etsy and eBay; short-form travel comedy is one of the most reliable viral content genres; commodity parts (ESP32-class MCU, MEMS IMU, MP3 decoder) make a sub-$20 landed device possible at 1,000-unit volume. Every figure is an unverified claim in Research; the documents give three other costs at volume, which are with engineering (WS14).

rows.appendBody: Phase 1, "Proof of funny", runs weeks 1-3: build the five units, film the hero set (a real suitcase talking back at a real check-in scale, the handler toss, the carousel laps), post unbranded and measure the share rate. The ask of about $750 is an estimate: its two parts, about $500 of parts and $200 of tooling, add up to $700. The documents use "EV batch" for three different things: these 5 validation units, the 20 units sent to creators, and a later run of 100.

rows.title: Success metrics: phase gate and launch
rows.body: Phase gate: a demo clip at 50k views, or 500 signups. Launch, if a crowdfunding launch runs: 2,000 backers, cost per customer under $8, visitor-to-backer conversion over 2.5%. Targets from the PRD; none is a forecast.

rows.title: Risk: batteries in checked bags, as it looks to others (High)
rows.body: Mitigation: AA alkaline only, by design; an off switch in case the airport asks; a carry-on use in the marketing.

rows.title: Risk: annoyance and airline complaints (Medium)
rows.body: Mitigation: governed output: 6 an hour at most, a 3 s cooldown, an 85 dBA ceiling, a volume button; and lines that are never about security and never aimed at the people nearby.

rows.title: Risk: imitators (Medium)
rows.body: Mitigation: speed, the brand and the voice; a design patent and a trademark; the classifier as a trade secret.

rows.title: Risk: voice rights and publicity claims (Medium)
rows.body: Mitigation: an original voice with a release, or a generated voice whose terms allow selling it; no celebrity impressions.

rows.title: Risk: seasonality, Q4-heavy (Low-Med)
rows.body: Mitigation: voice packs and holiday packs through the year; spring-break and summer editions; the wedding and group-trip angle.

rows.title: Risk: single-source audio module (Low)
rows.body: Mitigation: a second source for the audio module (YX5200 or KT148A); a later revision keeps the clips in flash and drops the module.

rows.title: Press angles on file (no release has been written)
rows.body: The documents hold three press lines and no release text. (1) PRD: "the world's sassiest suitcase". (2) Naming note: "the world's sassiest suitcase files its first claim". (3) Playbook, the local-news line for the Complaint Desk: "a suitcase filed a complaint at the airport today".

rows.title: Will TSA confiscate it?
rows.body: "Alkaline AA. No lithium. We checked." The playbook's answer went on: "The bag insists you switch it OFF before checking." That sentence is dropped: with AA cells the unit is not required to be off, and it has an off switch in case the airport asks. The battery rules are unverified claims in Research; check them before this is published.

rows.title: Can it ride in a checked bag?
rows.body: Yes: it runs on AA alkaline cells, never lithium, so it may stay on, and there is an off switch if anyone asks. The launch video's lower third says "AA POWER - checked-bag legal. No lithium, no drama." The rule itself is an unverified claim in Research.

rows.title: Will it annoy everyone around me?
rows.body: The governor allows one gag per kind of moment per journey phase, a 3 s cooldown and at most 6 gags an hour, at no more than 85 dBA at 1 m, with a volume button. The video's line: "6 GAGS/HOUR MAX - funny, not annoying".

rows.title: Does it need an app or pairing?
rows.body: No. No app, no pairing, one button; it runs on two AA cells (the launch video's host says three, which was the count before 22 Nov). The radios are disabled in firmware.

rows.title: How long do the batteries last?
rows.body: Not measured. The PRD stated 3-6 months on three AA cells; the unit now takes two, so engineering (WS14) estimates it again.

rows.title: Can I change what it says or how loud it is?
rows.body: One button: a short press cycles the volume (50 / 75 / 100%), a long press swaps the voice pack, a 10 s hold is a factory reset. More voice packs and holiday packs are sold as add-ons.

rows.title: What does it react to?
rows.body: Eight travel moments: a hard impact, the weigh-in, a handle grab, free-fall, the carousel, a conveyor or cart ride, being upside down, and hours untouched in the dark. The video's line: "8 REAL TRAVEL MOMENTS - detected, not scripted". More moments are proposed in the lines document.

rows.title: FAQ house style: the Complaint Department
rows.body: All support is in character ("Our agents are currently on a tarmac delay"), with the real answer under every joke; order lookup, returns, and the safety and battery page.

Working figure, not a decision: the two are not the same kind of number. $15k is the funding goal (the PRD's, and the low end of the first proposal's $15-20k); 2,000 backers, about $48k at a $24 average, is the playbook's target for the campaign. rows.appendBody: Three steps: "Where did your bag suffer?"; "What did they do to it?"; "Rate the trauma". Out comes a short audio complaint in the bag's voice and a claim ticket with a claim number; downloading or sharing asks for an email. A "Complaint of the Week" is featured, and the best complaint of the month wins a free unit. Nothing is public before moderation.

The mechanics, on the referral engine built into this app: 1 signup is "BOARDING GROUP D"; 3 referrals earn a free voice pack at launch ("upgrade to Group B"); 10 lock the early price ("Group A"); 25 earn the collector tier ("FIRST CLASS"). Every share message is written as a complaint from the user's bag. One referral per verified email.

rows.appendBody: Raw material the documents hold for whoever writes it: the one-liner; the eight moments and their lines; no app, no pairing, one button; two AA cells; voice packs and holiday packs; at most six gags an hour; a tag of 80 x 60 x 42 mm that hangs from the handle, with a name card and a tracker pocket; the PRD's brief, "tuned to gag travel gift keywords". Wording such as "checked-bag legal" needs checking against Amazon's rules and against the facts first. The Shame Ads are invented reviews and must never be used as customer reviews.

rows.setBody:
**Decided by the owner on 22 Nov 2026.** The product's own site runs on the stack this app is built on: Next.js, React, Tailwind and PostgreSQL with pgvector, with files and embeddings kept in PostgreSQL. Stripe takes payment on the site and the Amazon marketplace carries the listing; there is no Shopify. Mail goes out through the product's own mail server, whose SMTP details the admin enters in Admin, and referrals run on the engine built into this app. The unit takes two AA alkaline cells and uses the Adafruit MPU6050 breakout. It has an off switch in case the airport asks, though with AA cells it is not required to be off. It is a tag that hangs from the handle, 80 x 60 x 42 mm, with a name card and a tracker pocket, made as one integrated print that needs little work from the builder. The detection rules: free-fall is more than 0.3 s; the carousel is circular, periodic motion for about 15 s or more; a handle grab is tilt and quick motion, then sustained tilt plus steady carry; a hard impact is as the design package documents it. The marketing budget is 5,000 USD. More voice packs and holiday packs are to be sold.

**Decided in the documents.** Alkaline AA power, so the bag can talk in the hold. Radios off. No celebrity impressions. Voice packs on microSD, sold as add-ons. The governor: one gag per moment per phase, three seconds apart, six an hour at most. A cheap test before any launch money is spent.

**Estimated, because nobody knows yet.** A first build takes about 3.5 hours of hands-on work plus about 5 hours of unattended printing (the build guide's figure; the PRD's 90 minutes is the electronics alone). One prototype's parts add up to about $65: the parts list's 16 lines total $64.80, while the PRD's nine rows add up to $64.34 under the same printed total and its cost table's prototype column to $58.80. One printed tag is about 75 g of PETG, about $1.50 of filament. The ask of about $750 is itself an estimate.

**With engineering.** The firmware's details where the documents disagree (the history buffer, the sleep mode, the filter, the boot log, the weigh-in and conveyor rules), the sketch, which exists only inside a chat document and has not been compiled, the parts list for two AA cells and the tag, the costs at volume, and the wording of the card in the box.

**Still open, for the owner.**

- **The name.** Every document says Baggage Claims; the project is called Emotional Baggage; the naming note ranks Sass Case first for retail and warns that Emotional Baggage "attracts pre-existing novelty trademarks". No trademark or domain screen has been run.
- **A crowdfunding launch, or straight to the listing.** The documents plan a Kickstarter; the channels decided on 22 Nov are Amazon and the product's own site.
- **Who voices the bag.** A generated voice from this app's voice settings, a contracted voice actor, or one then the other.
- **The first market.** The United States alone, or with the EU.
- **The lines.** The owner's own lines are kept as he wrote them; proposals for every sensed moment, and for new moments, wait for his stars and strikes.
- **The packs.** Which come first, and what the New Yorker pack is called.

The look, the words on the tag and the launch line are being chosen from the design proposal.

rows.appendBody: House rules for every line, set on 22 Nov 2026: the bag is the butt of the joke and is never mean to the people nearby; nothing about security, weapons, bombs, hijacking or anything an airport could treat as a threat or a false alarm; nothing built on a stereotype of any group; no celebrity impressions; most lines under ten words. The owner's own lines are kept exactly as he wrote them. At least eight more lines are proposed for each of the eight sensed moments, with fifteen new moments the same hardware could sense, in docs/design/baggage-claims-lines.md; the first of each is listed below as a proposal, and none is chosen until the owner stars or strikes it. The launch script's "Three double-A batteries" becomes two.
